summary: Measured against the other Belgian bank pages in the set, ING reads clearly as a traditional bank (position score 0.21) and leads its peers on several dimensions at once: it quotes far more figures, is coded as designed mobile-first, targets students or young people, and scores highest on making the offer feel worth having. Its clearest weaknesses are calls to action (2.0 against a peer mean of 13.4) and the complete absence of a comparison table (0.0 against 0.38, where 38% of peer pages have one). The dataset contains no performance data and a single capture day (2026-09-21), so everything below is a hypothesis ING can test, not a proven effect.

recommendations.title: Add repeated calls to action across the current-account pages
recommendations.finding: Calls to action is ING's weakest measured signal: 2.0 against a peer mean of 13.4, roughly one standard deviation below the peer set (gap -1.06), and about one standard deviation below the market in ING's overall signature.
recommendations.recommendation: Place a clearly labelled call to action after each content block on the current-account and opening-account pages (hero, benefits, figures, footer), keeping identical wording and destination each time so the path stays consistent.

recommendations.title: Add a comparison table to the current-account pack pages
recommendations.finding: No ING page in the set includes a comparison table (0.0), while 38% of peer pages do — a gap of about 0.79 standard deviations.
recommendations.recommendation: Add a compact comparison table to the current-account pack page showing packs side by side (account, card, app features, fees, conditions), so visitors can compare without leaving the page. Keep it the same table on the French and Dutch versions.

recommendations.title: Reduce the density of figures and attach disclosure to each one
recommendations.finding: ING quotes far more figures and percentages than peers — 25.5 against a peer mean of 12.15, the largest single gap in the set at about 1.6 standard deviations, and roughly 1.4 standard deviations above the market overall.
recommendations.recommendation: Cut the number of separate figures per page to a short set of headline numbers and attach a plain-language conditions line to each one, so the volume of claims drops without losing the key rates. Test the trimmed version against the current page copy.

recommendations.title: Shorten the longest pages and fold detail into expandable blocks
recommendations.finding: ING's pages are among the longest measured: 9465 px against a peer mean of 6414.12 px (about 0.91 standard deviations above).
recommendations.recommendation: Move secondary detail (conditions, fee schedules, long benefit lists) into expandable sections or into the new comparison table, and shorten the opening blocks so the main offer and its call to action sit higher on the page.

recommendations.title: Make the fast sign-up promise specific
recommendations.finding: ING more often promises fast digital sign-up than peers (0.5 against 0.15, about 0.96 standard deviations above) and it is one of the few banks coded as designed mobile-first (1.0 against 0.38). Both signals are above the peer set but are model- and rubric-based judgements.
recommendations.recommendation: Next to the main call to action on the opening-account page, state what fast sign-up means in concrete terms — how many steps, what the customer needs at hand, and how long it typically takes — rather than leaving the promise unqualified.

recommendations.title: Give the student and young-audience message its own path
recommendations.finding: ING targets students or young people far more often than peers (1.0 against 0.38, about 1.26 standard deviations above), making this one of its clearest distinguishing signals.
recommendations.recommendation: Keep the student and young-audience copy on the dedicated jeunes page and add its own call to action plus a short 'what you need to open it' block there, instead of mixing that message into the general current-account copy.

recommendations.title: Reuse the strongest offer framing on the pages that lack it
recommendations.finding: ING's campaign structure is more complete than peers' (AIDA coverage 3.5 against 2.71) and it consistently makes the offer feel worth having (desire 1.0 against 0.43). The weak stage is the action step, not the desire step.
recommendations.recommendation: Reuse ING's existing desire-led block as a template on the pages that currently lack one (savings, term account, mortgage) and close each block with a single, repeated call to action rather than a bare rate statement.

recommendations.title: Test lower-brightness backgrounds with stronger contrast
recommendations.finding: ING's pages are brighter than peers (0.9 against 0.72), and brightness is the single strongest split in the dataset between traditional and challenger banks (0.86 against 0.45). Brightness is a stylistic dimension with no measured link to any outcome here.
recommendations.recommendation: Run a small A/B test on the hero and section backgrounds of the main current-account and brand pages, using a darker background with higher text and button contrast, and keep it only if it does not hurt readability.

recommendations.title: Have the opening-account pages comparison-ready before the late-summer window
recommendations.finding: Revolut shows a sustained search-interest anomaly in the Belgian neobank brand cluster from 2026-08-02 to 2026-09-13, with weekly values of 9, 9, 9, 10, 9 and 19 and 26 flagged anomalies in the export. This is attention to a competitor brand, not evidence that any page or campaign worked; the hypothesis to verify is that ING's opening-account page is the one visitors compare during such windows.
recommendations.recommendation: Have ING's opening-account and current-account pages in a comparison-ready state (packs, fees, what is included, switching steps) by the end of July, so no page edit is needed mid-window.
recommendations.market_context: Sustained search-interest anomaly for the term Revolut in the neobank brand cluster, running 2026-08-02 to 2026-09-13 with weekly values from 9 to 19 and 26 anomalies in the export. The link between that attention and ING's pages is a hypothesis, not a proven effect.

recommendations.title: Sequence switching and account-transfer content around peer migration periods
recommendations.finding: Crelan shows a sustained search-interest anomaly in the traditional-bank brand cluster between 2024-12-15 and 2025-07-06, with weekly values between 30 and 33, following the merger with AXA Bank Belgium and the migration of about 840,000 clients on 2024-06-10. Peer attention is not evidence about ING's pages, and the export contains no campaign matched to a spike.
recommendations.recommendation: Keep ING's account-switching and bring-your-account-over content on the current-account page live and current ahead of peer migration milestones, when customers of other banks are most likely to be looking; treat the timing link as a hypothesis to verify before committing budget.
recommendations.market_context: Sustained search-interest anomaly for the term Crelan in the traditional-bank brand cluster, 2024-12-15 to 2025-07-06, weekly values 30 to 33, against the documented merger and client migration of 2024-06-10.

recommendations.title: Keep a standing short neobank comparison block ready for recurring spikes
recommendations.finding: bunq shows six isolated spikes, all at value 1, on 2025-03-16, 2025-05-25, 2025-09-14, 2025-11-23, 2026-02-15 and 2026-07-26 in the neobank brand cluster, with seven flagged anomalies. The values are small and recurring and no campaign is matched to them in the export.
recommendations.recommendation: Keep a permanent, short neobank comparison block on the current-account page so ING never has to publish a rushed edit during one of these short spikes; the recurring pattern is a hypothesis, not a proven trigger for a page change.
recommendations.market_context: Six isolated search-interest spikes for the term bunq in the neobank brand cluster, each at value 1, spread between 2025-03-16 and 2026-07-26, with seven anomalies flagged in the export.

recommendations.title: Keep ING's leadership claims specific rather than broad
recommendations.finding: Of ING's 23 headlines in the last 90 days, sustainability is the largest theme at 6 and financial results is next at 5, while digital innovation accounts for 3; notable headlines include the Milieudefensie climate case against ING and ING's financing of three oil companies. If ING's brand and account pages lean on a broad digital or sustainability leadership claim, the current coverage does not echo it at the same weight — a hypothesis ING should verify against its own claim wording.
recommendations.recommendation: On the pourquoi-ing and current-account pages, replace any broad 'leader' statement with a specific, dated, verifiable claim about what the app or the account actually does.
recommendations.reputation_context: ING's last-90-day themes: esg_sustainability 6, financial_results 5, innovation_digital 3, product_launch 3, regulatory 3, crisis_or_scandal 1 and other 3, across 23 headlines, including coverage of the Milieudefensie climate case and ING's financing of three oil companies.

recommendations.title: Keep urgency framing away from sustainability and rate-disclosure blocks
recommendations.finding: Sustainability (6 of 23 headlines) and crisis or scandal (1 of 23) appear in ING's last-90-day themes, and notable headlines cover a climate case against ING and its financing of oil companies. Heavy urgency or scarcity language next to sustainability and rate-disclosure content risks reading as a mismatch with that coverage; the link to any page effect is a hypothesis to verify.
recommendations.recommendation: On the savings and term-account pages, move promotional urgency away from the sustainability and rate-disclosure blocks and give those blocks a plain, factual presentation with their own explanation line.
recommendations.reputation_context: ING's last-90-day headline themes include esg_sustainability (6 of 23) and crisis_or_scandal (1 of 23), with notable headlines on the Milieudefensie climate case and ING's financing of three oil companies.

recommendations.title: State price and conditions in the same block as the headline offer
recommendations.finding: Regulatory is one of ING's last-90-day themes at 3 of 23 headlines, whose notable examples cover ING raising tariffs and pressure on its earnings model. This says what ING is in the news about, nothing about how any page performed.
recommendations.recommendation: On the current-account and opening-account pages, put the price, the eligibility conditions and what changes after any promotional period in the same block as the headline offer, rather than further down the page.
recommendations.reputation_context: ING's last-90-day themes include regulatory at 3 of 23 headlines, with a notable headline on ING raising tariffs while AI pressure weighs on its earnings model.
